h1: SEO Agency in Pune: Chakan factories and Hinjewadi software
metaTitle: SEO Agency in Pune: Manufacturing and IT, Separately
metaDescription: Pune runs two economies: Chakan manufacturing and Hinjewadi IT. Each needs its own keyword set. Plus a 90-day guarantee against your own baseline.
answer: Pune is two disconnected markets sharing one search results page. Chakan and Pimpri industrial buyers search part numbers, grades and certifications. Hinjewadi IT firms chase evaluators in Chicago and Stuttgart. One keyword strategy fails both, and a ₹75,000 retainer split evenly across them under-funds both halves.
takeaways: The industrial belt around **Chakan, Talegaon and Pimpri-Chinchwad** is one of India's densest automotive and engineering clusters. Its buyers search specifications, not adjectives.
You will not out-rank IndiaMART on a generic category term. You beat it on specificity — grades, tolerances, certifications, drawings.
**Hinjewadi** IT firms are doing international SEO, not local SEO. Their buyers never type "Pune".
Marathi matters in Pune consumer and local search in a way it doesn't for B2B industrial or export IT.
Roughly a third of a retainer — technical, speed, schema, indexation — serves both audiences at once. Only the content and link budget genuinely has to be split.

sections.h2: Two economies, one search results page
body: Pune is unusual among Indian metros in having two large, prosperous, entirely unrelated commercial bases. Northwest, the Chakan–Talegaon–Pimpri-Chinchwad MIDC belt is one of the country's biggest automotive and engineering manufacturing clusters, with global carmakers and a deep tier-one and tier-two supplier base. West, Hinjewadi's Rajiv Gandhi Infotech Park holds Pune's IT services concentration, selling engineering hours to North America and Europe.

They share a city, a talent pool and a traffic problem. They share nothing in search behaviour. It goes wrong when an agency runs one playbook across both — usually the one it's most comfortable with — and reports on whichever audience happened to respond.

sections.h2: Beating IndiaMART without trying to out-rank it
body: Every industrial SEO conversation in Pune hits the same wall. You search your category and the first page is marketplaces. That won't change, and treating it as the objective wastes a year.

The way through is structural. A marketplace listing is a template: company name, category, location, price band. It can't host a materials table, a tolerance chart, a process capability description or a page explaining why a grade fails in a given application. Your site can host all of them, and each matches a query the directory has no page for.
numbered: **One page per process, not one for "our capabilities".** CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, pressure die casting, heat treatment — each is a query and each deserves its own URL with real parameters.
**Publish certifications as content, not a logo strip.** Buyers search standards by name. A page explaining what your IATF 16949 or ISO 9001 scope covers ranks and qualifies at once.

**Put the specification in the text.** Grades, sizes, ranges, machine bed dimensions, batch minimums. Sourcing engineers search in these exact terms, and most supplier sites bury them in a PDF that Google reads badly and buyers read never.
**Answer the failure questions.** "Why does [material] crack in [process]" is a query a directory will never rank for and a supplier who knows the answer always can.
**Track the phone.** Most industrial enquiries in Pune arrive by call or WhatsApp. If reporting only counts form fills, the work looks broken while the office phone rings.

callout.title: The RFQ measurement trap
callout.body: Industrial deal cycles frequently run past a quarter, and the first search-driven enquiry may be a request for a quote on one part. Judge it on enquiry count and quote value, not on closed orders inside 90 days — anyone guaranteeing you closed orders on that cycle hasn't read your business.

sections.h2: Hinjewadi is doing international SEO, not Pune SEO
body: If your clients are in Chicago, Stuttgart or Amsterdam, ranking for "software company in Pune" is worth roughly nothing to pipeline. That query is typed by candidates, local vendors and competitors doing research. The job is ranking inside another country's result set from an Indian address, and that's a different technical brief.
bullets: **Domain choice comes first.** A `.in` carries an India signal, and Google retired the country-targeting control in Search Console, so nothing overrides it. Generic domains — `.com`, `.io` — are geographically neutral.
**Filter Search Console by country before judging performance.** An unfiltered report on an Indian-linked site will be India-heavy and tells you nothing about buyer visibility.
**Set your rank tracker to the target market.** Checking positions from a Hinjewadi desk on an Indian Google account shows India's results, not your buyer's.

**Links decide it.** If every referring domain is a `.in` directory, you read as an Indian business. Earning coverage on domains already appearing in your buyer's results is the slow, expensive half of international SEO — the half cheap packages skip.
**Write in the buyer's phrasing.** Not translation, vocabulary. A German engineering buyer's words for the same service aren't your Indian sales deck's words.

sections.h2: Marathi, English, and where the language mix really shows up
body: Pune is a Marathi-language stronghold in a way that Mumbai, with its wider mix, is not. Whether it matters depends on which of Pune's two economies you're in.

For industrial B2B and export IT it doesn't. Sourcing engineers search specifications in English because the specifications are written in English, and a buyer in Stuttgart isn't searching in Marathi.

For consumer-facing categories — retail, clinics, real estate, education, home services — it genuinely does, though rarely as a full Marathi website. Most demand arrives as Romanised Marathi or code-mixed queries with English nouns inside Marathi structure, and Google treats each variant as a different query string. Tools under-report these badly, so your own Search Console report beats anything you'd pay for.
bullets: **Read your unfiltered Search Console queries** going back a year. Your real Marathi and Romanised-Marathi demand is already in there.
**Match the words back rather than translating forward.** Use the exact transliterated forms customers type, not a formal translation nobody searches.
**Don't commission a parallel Marathi site** unless you can staff it permanently. A half-maintained language version is a duplicate-content problem with a growth label on it.

sections.h2: Admission season, and the demand spike an education city hands you
body: Pune has one of India's largest concentrations of universities, engineering colleges and management institutes, with a student population arriving from across the country. That produces a demand pattern most Pune businesses under-use, and it isn't only relevant to educational institutions.

Intake windows create sharp, predictable, annually repeating spikes — course and fee queries, obviously, but also flats and PG accommodation, second-hand furniture, gyms, tiffin services and every category a few hundred thousand new arrivals need in the same fortnight. The discipline here is scheduling, not writing.
numbered: **Pull last year's seasonality from your own Search Console**, month by month, for the queries that matter. The pattern repeats closely enough to plan against.
**Publish one to two quarters before the spike.** A page needs to be indexed, linked and settled before demand arrives. Commissioning content when enquiries start rising means missing the intake.
**Refresh, don't republish.** The page that ranked last intake usually beats a new one. Update dates and fees on the existing URL and keep its history.
**Publish the numbers competitors hide.** Fee ranges, eligibility, deposit terms, refund policy. In admission search the honest page wins, because so few exist.

sections.h2: Splitting one retainer across two audiences, honestly
body: The question Pune founders ask most: we sell to both, can you cover both for ₹75,000 a month? The honest answer is partly.

About a third of a retainer serves every audience at once. Site speed, crawlability, indexation, schema, internal linking, analytics and call tracking, Google Business Profile — none of that cares who your buyer is. That's why two audiences on one site isn't as inefficient as it sounds.

The other two-thirds — keyword research, content, digital PR — can't be shared. Industrial specification pages and US-facing capability pages need different writers, different research and different outreach targets. Split that evenly and you get two half-funded programmes, neither beating a baseline. That's not an upsell; it's why engagements like this fail in month five. So we do one of three things, and say which before you sign.
bullets: **Sequence it.** Fund one audience properly for two quarters until it compounds without full attention, then stage the second. Slower on paper, and the only version that reliably works at ₹75,000.
**Fund two.** If both revenue lines are material they need something closer to two retainers, and we'll say so rather than quietly delivering half of each.
**Decline.** If both are urgent and the budget is one retainer, we're the wrong agency for at least one of them, and pretending otherwise puts our own guarantee at risk.
**Whichever we pick, the baseline is per-audience.** Blending industrial enquiries and IT leads into one number lets an agency hide a failure inside a success.

callout.title: The guarantee, stated exactly
callout.body: We freeze your trailing-90-day qualified organic leads on day one, from your CRM. If we haven't beaten that number in 90 days, we keep working free until we do. Never a ranking position for a keyword — nobody controls the index. See [what SEO costs in India](/cost/seo-cost-in-india) for what changes the number, or [our SEO page](/seo) for scope.

faqs.q: How much does an SEO agency in Pune cost?
faqs.a: Packages advertise from roughly ₹10,000 a month to ₹2,00,000+ for enterprise scope. Below about ₹25,000 you're buying part-time junior attention rather than a team. We start at ₹75,000/mo ex-GST, with smaller sites from ₹40,000, month-to-month after the first quarter.

faqs.q: Can SEO work for a manufacturing company in Chakan or Pimpri?
faqs.a: Yes, but not on generic category terms — IndiaMART and TradeIndia own those and you won't displace them. It works on specificity: processes, material grades, tolerances, certification scope, machine capability, application failure questions. And it only shows in reporting if you track phone and WhatsApp enquiries.

faqs.q: Do I need Marathi content to rank in Pune?
faqs.a: For industrial B2B or export IT, no. For consumer-facing categories it matters, but usually as Romanised Marathi and code-mixed queries rather than a full Marathi site. Your own Search Console query report is a better guide to this than any keyword tool.

faqs.q: We sell to both local industry and overseas clients. Can one retainer cover both?
faqs.a: Partly. Around a third of the work — technical, speed, indexation, analytics — serves both at once. Content and link building can't be shared. At ₹75,000 we'd sequence the two rather than split the budget evenly, because an even split under-funds both and neither beats its baseline.

faqs.q: How long does SEO take for a Pune IT company selling to the US?
faqs.a: Longer than domestic SEO, because the constraint is link relevance in the buyer's market and links build slowly. Expect the first quarter to be structural — domain, hreflang, measurement, page inventory — with visible movement in filtered US impressions after that, not before.

Movement against your own frozen baseline: your trailing-90-day qualified organic leads from your CRM, agreed in writing on day one. Miss it in 90 days and we keep working at no charge until we beat it. We never guarantee a ranking position, and we track each audience's baseline separately.
